quizName: DMV Practice Test #13 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: To avoid confusing other drivers, you should:

options.text: Turn off your turn signal when you finish turning or changing lanes.
Use your horn only in emergencies.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your turn signal when you finish turning or changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Turn off your turn signal after you finish turning or changing lanes. Leaving it on confuses other drivers about where you are going.

questions.question: The center portion of a lane has an oily strip. This strip:

options.text: Should be avoided at all times.
Usually has good traction for riding, unless it is raining.
Should only be used if you are sharing the lane with another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually has good traction for riding, unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: The oily center strip usually provides enough grip for safe riding, unless it rains. The strip is usually less than two feet wide, so riders can ride on either side of it and stay in the center lane.

questions.question: When positioning yourself on the motorcycle:

options.text: You should use your arms to hold yourself up.
You should use your arms to steer the motorcycle.
You should have to reach to hold the handgrips.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should use your arms to steer the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Use good riding posture by steering with your arms instead of holding yourself up. Sit so your elbows are slightly bent when you hold the handgrips.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They warn drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the right lane will end.

questions.question: Oil drippings and debris often collect in ______ of a lane.
questions.explanation: Oil drippings and debris from vehicles collect in the center of the lane.

questions.question: Shifting gears while turning:

options.text: Should only be done if you can do it smoothly.
Is better than shifting before the turn.
Is the best way to control your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should only be done if you can do it smoothly.
questions.explanation: Shift gears before turning whenever possible. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly. A sudden power change to the rear wheel can cause a skid.

questions.question: Small vehicles appear to be ________ and slower than they really are.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast a small vehicle is going or how far away it is. Do not assume that drivers of larger vehicles can accurately see your speed and location.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They warn drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that traffic ahead will merge.

questions.question: When parked on the road, a motorcycle should:

options.text: Be at an angle of 45 to 90 degrees from the curb.
Be parked without touching the curb.
Be parked parallel to the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be at an angle of 45 to 90 degrees from the curb.
questions.explanation: Park your motorcycle at an angle of 45 to 90 degrees from the curb. A wheel or fender should touch the curb.

questions.question: If you need to react to a hazard, do not:

options.text: Alert other drivers by using your horn, lights, or signals.

questions.explanation: Let other drivers know you are there by using your horn, lights, and signals. Adjust your speed for the situation. Change your lane position or direction as needed.

questions.question: When riding, you should check your rearview mirror:
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often while riding. Also check them before changing lanes, when stopping at an intersection, and before slowing down.

questions.question: At an uncontrolled intersection, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, who should yield?

options.text: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlights to signal the other vehicle to go.
Go through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or traffic lights, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle well, you should:

options.text: Use your arms to hold yourself up.
Keep your knees against the gas tank.
Sit so your arms are straight when holding the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank.
questions.explanation: Sit so your arms can steer, not support your body. Your elbows should be slightly bent. Press your knees against the gas tank to help you balance.

questions.question: An engine will seize because of:
questions.explanation: Without enough oil, the engine's parts cannot move smoothly. This causes the engine to overheat and seize.

questions.question: When turning, what should you do with your head?

options.text: Move your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn just your head to look through the turn.
Turn your head and shoulders to look through the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head to look through the turn.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn to see where you are going. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level. Turning your shoulders can cause you to steer off course.

questions.question: You should increase your following distance when:
questions.explanation: Give yourself more distance to stop on slippery pavement. Also increase your distance if you cannot see ahead clearly or if traffic is heavy.

questions.question: While riding, you should wear:

options.text: Earplugs to protect your hearing from engine and wind noise.
A helmet to protect your hearing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Earplugs to protect your hearing from engine and wind noise.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise while riding can damage your hearing over time, even with a full-face helmet. Use earplugs to prevent this damage.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, a motorcyclist should NOT:

options.text: Choose a lane position where other drivers can see you.
Have your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.

questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that is most visible. Have your hands ready on the clutch and both brakes. Slow down when approaching. Do not change speed or position suddenly, as this confuses other drivers.

questions.question: To swerve correctly, you should:

options.text: Press the handgrip toward the direction you want to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip toward the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve away from danger, press on the handgrip on the side where you want to escape.

questions.question: Helmets are:
questions.explanation: Georgia law requires all riders to wear a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards. A helmet is your best protection against head and neck injuries in an accident.

questions.question: A motorcycle's horn is ________ a passenger vehicle's horn.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle horn is not as loud as a car horn. Riders should use their horn when needed, but should not depend on it for safety.

questions.question: When making a normal stop on a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop normally, use the front and rear brakes together. Also downshift as you brake.

questions.question: To turn safely on a motorcycle, you should always:

options.text: Lean toward the direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean toward the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: Always lean in the direction you are turning. Slow down before you enter the turn, not during it.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, how does a motorcycle respond to steering changes?
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to the motorcycle. The extra weight makes the motorcycle slower to speed up, slow down, and turn.

questions.question: Where is there the greatest risk of conflict between a motorcycle and other vehicles?
questions.explanation: Intersections are where conflicts between motorcycles and other vehicles happen most often. Riders must be careful when approaching an intersection.
